outcome.technical: (1) Where a call's reading lives: one file per call under the state directory, journal-preimage-<writer key>.<first 20 hex of sha256(tool_use_id)>.json (_config.CALL_READING_FILE, _config._call_reading_path). The id reaches the name only through the digest (cr5: an id spelling ../../ stays in the state directory). Written by _config.record_call_reading only when the pass before read the switch on (a missing config reads as on), and only when the payload names a call id. Its body is the config as that pass found it (path, ts, sha256, content), the id and journalOn true. journal-writes._keep_reading writes it on the sweep lane (Bash, MCP) for the project's config, and on the edit lane for a write whose target is CONFIG_REL, in the tree the slot is in. The pass after reads its own (_own_reading -> _config.call_reading), then removes it (_config.drop_call_reading). (2) Two calls of one writer: the per-writer start record and the per-writer, per-path slot were both replaceable. So with the switch off now, the config is judged against the call's own pre-image, not the writer's slot. That is why each call open across the flip leaves a row: without it, the first pass after refreshes the shared slot past the flip and the second sees no move (mutation rows 7 and 8 show this). (3) Leftover rule: a reading whose pass after never runs keeps the journal-preimage- prefix, so detect-plan-skip.py's _gc_state, which runs at each prompt, removes it once its mtime is older than _GC_MAX_AGE (cr5 drives the real function: kept an hour on, removed past the bound). An ordinary call pays nothing for that rule, since no directory listing runs on a tool call. What it does pay with the journal on: on the swept Pre, one more read of the config and one small write; on the Post, one unlink. With the journal off at Post, one more read. A leftover is never another call's reading because its name is that call's id digest (and writer key). No reading is written while the switch is off. (4) journalOn left the shared call-start record: record_call_start lost its journal_on argument, and the record is {at, toolUseId} again, the shape guard-bash-writes reads (call_start, window_peers unchanged). cw7 was re-pinned on purpose. It used to assert that the reading rides in the start record's one write and reads back on only for its call. It now asserts that the record holds exactly {at, toolUseId}, that call_journal_on is False with no reading, and that a reading survives a later call's start record. (5) Edit lane, driven with two Writes of one session on the config (probe_editlane in the scratch directory). Before, PreF PreW PostW flip PostF gave rows=1: W's 'Write wrote' and no flip row, with a verify warning. PreW PreF PostW flip PostF gave the same. PreF PreW flip PostF PostW gave 1 flip row. PreF flip PreW PostW PostF gave 1. After, the counts are 2 (W's write row plus F's flip), 2, 2 flip rows and 1, with no warnings. So it lost the row, and it is fixed under the same rule. sn21 holds it. (6) Probes on this tree. probe_flight: A=2, B=1, C=2, D=1, E=2, F=2, G=2, H=1; before it was A1 B0 C1 D0 E1 F1 G2 H1. probe_open, probe_nopost and probe_spell are identical to the orchestrator's before outputs (diff empty). rows_on gives identical JSON for the export and this tree. probe_guard gives the same verdicts; the only difference is the record keys, ['at','journalOn','toolUseId'] -> ['at','toolUseId']. verify_all, run from a mirrored copy: nine ok, plus probe_j BAD on u3b only (the known one). (7) Bench. The bench-hooks.py --gate exit code was 0. bench-hooks measure() with hooks_dir pointed at matched scratch copies (journal-writes, edit lane), two runs each: before 69.38 ms and 87.71 ms, after 88.83 ms and 67.33 ms. That is noise, and this lane writes no reading. The swept Bash Pre and Post as processes, journal on, n=31 medians, two runs each: before Pre 136.2/139.9 ms and Post 138.6/138.3 ms; after Pre 131.7/138.5 ms and Post 132.6/137.9 ms. The state file count afterwards was the same, so no reading was left behind. (8) Suites: the eight dependants were swept with --jobs 4, exit code 0. test__config 419, test__journal_io 282, test_audit_journal 186, test_guard_bash_writes 239, test_guard_edits 131, test_hooks 247, test_journal_writes 207 and test_require_plan 245 cases all came back ok. test__deps, test__output_lints and test__refs were swept with exit code 0. gate-parity exited 0, prove-gates --list exited 0, ruff exited 0, and vermin -t=3.8- exited 0. run-test-gate for SG1 --task SG1.51-ukq, without --record, printed GATE GREEN. (9) Dependants. _config.py is imported by every hook. The only API changes are record_call_start dropping journal_on (its one caller, journal-writes, is updated) and the new call_reading, record_call_reading and drop_call_reading functions; call_journal_on keeps its signature. guard-bash-writes is unchanged in what it reads, and its suite passes (239 ok). test_guard_edits, test_hooks, test_require_plan, test__journal_io and test_audit_journal are still correct and green. tests/test_journal_writes.py and tests/test__config.py are changed as described. In SECURITY.md, item 3's switch-off sentences were rewritten and no fail-mode table row changed; test_hooks' quoted phrase is untouched. README, the build guide and CHANGELOG were rewritten as below. The other dependants listed in the brief (scripts, tools, eval files) neither read the changed functions nor quote the changed sentences. tools/sweep-selftests.py does not need a row: its existing journal-preimage row matches the new name for a main agent and for a subagent (checked against _LIVE_WRITES_RE). (10) Document sentences, in SECURITY.md item 3, the README journal paragraph, the build guide's 'The last will reaches the trail' and the CHANGELOG Unreleased Security bullet. First: a switch-off by hand or in the panel between calls leaves no row and the trail check does not see it (sn20: by hand, verify gives no finding and no warning naming the config; sn4: in the panel). Second: one that lands while a call is open is recorded under that call; the row says in whose window the switch went off, not whose hand did it (sn20: a command's row under sess-a, a subagent's MCP read's row under agent0007). Third: a switch-off by a call whose pass after never runs leaves no row (sn22: a command and an edit tool). No claim is made about when the host skips the pass after. SECURITY.md's sentence 'the trail check still warns about the hand edit (sn1-sn7)' was narrowed to 'a hand edit an edit tool later rewrote (sn3)', because a hand flip followed only by commands draws no warning (sn20).
outcome.descriptive: A call's reading of the journal switch, with its config pre-image, is now kept per call, so a second call of the same writer can no longer take the switch-off row away on any lane; the documents now say whose row a switch-off between calls, inside an open call's window, and by a call with no pass after is.
